verdict.rationale: A live probe confirms Mirrors publishes an llms.txt at https://mirrors.dev/llms.txt (HTTP 200). It contains an agent-readable product summary and content about corrections and how they fit with observability and eval tools, so a user can point an agent at it. The docs also say a coding agent can write corrections. missing for 10: a markdown version of the docs (https://mirrors.dev/docs.md returns 404), evidence that llms.txt covers the full docs in depth (e.g., an llms-full.txt), and independent or hands-on confirmation that agents consume it well.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can point an agent at llms.txt or agent-oriented docs

citations.quote: PROBE llms.txt: HTTP 200 at https://mirrors.dev/llms.txt # Mirrors
Observability shows what an agent did, evals test a change, and corrections change what it gets in one situation. How they fit with Langfuse, LangSmith and Braintrust.
You or your coding agent write the correction and choose when to activate it.
